svg.title: ProcessForge distribution, workplace and project ownership
svg.desc: The distribution supplies shared Core and definitions. The workplace supplies registered resources and optional Runtime. CLI, host-owned MCP and optional app-server are separate adapters. Each project keeps its own context, exact Work contracts, evidence and private SQLite journals. These are ownership layers, not required physical directory nesting.
svg.text: Shared Core, separate owners
Ownership layers on one device or runner host; no required directory nesting or global .agents path.
ProcessForge distribution
bin/pf.py and shared Python Core
Official processes, schemas, templates and documentation
A linked project calls this installation; it does not copy Core.
Workplace: machine-local resources
Registries, knowledge roots, tools, templates and local config
Shared search index; Agent Ledger; optional Runtime state
Availability is distinct from a project's selected authorization.
Entry adapters use the shared Core
CLI: short-lived commands
MCP: independent host-owned stdio
App-server: optional PF Runtime
Project A: its own .pf/
Manifest, current context and selected resource references
Pinned Work, assignments, capsules and durable evidence
Artifacts, reviews and handoffs
Private runtime: events.sqlite3, hooks.sqlite3 and transcripts
Project B: its own .pf/
Independent context, scope and exact Work identities
Its own evidence and private project journals
Local launcher routes to the shared distribution
No copied Core or heavy workplace documentation trees
File-only Garage work needs no running app-server. The MCP host independently owns its connected process.
